newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian bank industry report ready on time.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian bank industry report ready on time.

text.p: The chairman of the Australian financial industry inquiry, Stan Wallis, said on Sunday that he believes his report will be handed to the government on schedule at the end of next month.
Industry analysts and commentators predict the report will trigger a wave of bank takeovers by recommending much greater deregulation of the sector.
"We will meet the 31st March deadline. I'm very confident of that as I sit here today," Wallis said in an interview on the Nine Network's Business Sunday programme.
Wallis, the former managing director of paper and packaging group Amcor Ltd and the head of the chief executive-based Business Council of Australia, was not asked about the contents of his report.

"It's coming together. We're getting through the big ticket issues and there is a lot of material to be prepared and written when you are producing a report of the nature that we're involved," he said.

The inquiry has received submissions from the banking, financial and insurance sectors about changes to regulatory framework, which now prevents mega-mergers between the major banks and life offices and also frowns on takeovers of the regional banks that specialise in home loans.

Among their widespread tips for industry rationalisation, analysts have constantly pointed to the likelihood that National Australia Bank Ltd will launch a takeover of fellow "big four" bank Westpac Banking Corp once the Wallis report is handed down.
Alternatively, they said NAB could bid for regional bank St George Bank Ltd, a Sydney-based group that recently acquired Advance Bank Ltd for more than A$2.5 billion in cash and shares.
